thread:
Alex (Recruiting Ops): Heads up — saw 3 double-bookings this morning. Interviewers updated availability but scheduler still showed old slots for ~15m.
Maria (People Ops): Ugh. Any pattern? Same timezone or all over?
Alex (Recruiting Ops): All across regions but same flow: interviewer edits availability in the UI -> Confirmation shows updated slots -> calendar still had old avail for a bit and candidates got invites.
Liam (Hiring Manager): Had one candidate accept a time that conflicted with another meeting. Not great.
Devon (Platform): Looking at logs now. I can see lots of 200s on the API but a flurry of cache misses later. Possible cache invalidation lag.
Devon (Platform): stack excerpt: `GET /v1/availability?user_id=U123` -> cached=true timestamp=1700001000 -> returned stale until invalidation at 1700001900 (90s later).
Alex (Recruiting Ops): We expect updates to reflect within <5s in scheduler.
Devon (Platform): Found config: `availability_cache_ttl_sec: 900` in prod-config (was supposed to be 30 for interactive updates). Looks like a deploy toggled to a high TTL.
Maria (People Ops): Is the config change recent? Who pushed it?
Devon (Platform): It went out in canary last night as part of redis tuning: commit 9f3a2b. I think intended to target batch report cache, but key names overlapped.
Alex (Recruiting Ops): Oof. That explains it. Can we scope the keyspace so interactive availability uses a different TTL?
Devon (Platform): Yes. Quick fix: change `availability:interactive:ttl` to 30s and leave `availability:reporting:ttl` at 900s. I can push a rollback for the config key now.
scheduler-bot: deploy started for svc-scheduler config-toggle (canary)
Maria (People Ops): Please coordinate — we need a communication note to recruiting and hiring managers if this will take a few mins.
Devon (Platform): Rolling out small config change to canary then global if green. I'll monitor conflicts metric (double_bookings_count).
Alex (Recruiting Ops): Can you also add a short retry on write so that UI-confirmation waits for cache invalidation for a max of 5s? Safer UX.
Devon (Platform): Good idea — add a `cache-warm` path: after availability update, call `invalidate` then read-back with up to 5s backoff. I'll file a tiny PR.
Liam (Hiring Manager): Appreciate the quick responses. Let me know when fixed so I can rescind the wrong invites.
Devon (Platform): Update: canary config applied at 2712345680, monitoring looks clean. Double bookings metric down to baseline. Will push global at 2712345688 if no regressions.
Alex (Recruiting Ops): Thanks — after global push can you post the rollback plan and the exact commit hash?
Devon (Platform): Yes: rollforward commit 9f3a2b -> patch commit b4f7c1 (scoped keys). Rollback is trivial: revert to previous config. I'll post PR link when merged.
Maria (People Ops): I'll send a quick note to recruiting and hiring managers summarizing impact and remediation.
Alex (Recruiting Ops): 👍 please include instructions for rescinding invites and a short apology template.
Devon (Platform): Global rollout done at 2712345689. Metrics stable. Closing the thread once PR is merged.
scheduler-bot: deploy succeeded for svc-scheduler config-toggle (global)
Maria (People Ops): PR posted and brief sent.
Alex (Recruiting Ops): Closing — thanks everyone.
